text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: cont-batch kvcache amplification in us-east-1. Elevated 5xx and latency on /v1/generate for multiple hosted customers. Auto-page to oncall-jordan and eng-runtime.

oncall-jordan: Ack. I'm on it. Seeing spike starting ~1730000500. 95p latency ~2.3s, error rate ~6% overall but higher for a few tenants (t-123, t-77).

oncall-jordan: Quick snapshot from metrics:
```
htop: mem pressure on gpu-nodes-6/7, kv_cache_evictions/sec: 18k, in-flight-batches: 1200, avg_batch_tokens: 12k
error: downstream timeout 504 from cont-batcher at 1730000589
```

devlin: likely continuous-batching misconfig. I see a recent flag rollout from ~1729999000 that set: `max_batch_tokens=20480` and `max_num_seqs=64` to squeeze throughput for a bulk customer test. That combination can blow up kvcache size and cause eviction storms.

ash: ? can we clamp quickly to reduce working set. Suggest rollback or hotfix to safer defaults: `max_batch_tokens=4096` `max_num_seqs=8`.

samir: Agreed. Hotpatch plan: 1) reduce max_batch_tokens globally in us-east policy, 2) set max_num_seqs cap, 3) enable per-route cap for the noisy tenants, 4) fallback model variant if timeouts persist.

maria: I'm drafting a short status for affected customers. Need ETA for mitigation.

devlin: I'll run the config change now. Pushing to config service.

devlin: `curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://config.internal.api/v1/contbatch/policies/us-east -d '{"max_batch_tokens":4096, "max_num_seqs":8}'`

(devlin posts) devlin: Pushed, returning 202. Rolling to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 90s.

sre-bot: deploy: contbatch-policy-rollout us-east -> 10% succeeded (50 nodes).

oncall-jordan: seeing immediate drop in 95p from 2.3s -> 750ms on batch directors at 1730000952. Error rate down to ~2.1%.

ash: OK good. Next, for tenants with sustained higher errors, setting route-level concurrency cap. I'll apply per-tenant token cap for t-123 and t-77.

devlin: Applying route caps:
```
PATCH /v1/routes/t-123/config
{ "batching": { "max_batch_tokens": 2048, "max_concurrent_batches": 4 } }
```

(devlin posts) devlin: route caps applied. Observed immediate drop in 500s for t-123.

ops-lead: Can we also disable prefix KV caching temporarily for us-east to prevent rehydration storms? That will increase per-token cost but reduce memory churn.

samir: Good idea. We can flip `kv_prefix_cache=false` on the runtime feature-gate. I'll do a staged flip across the pool.

samir: `PATCH /internal/flags/contbatch?region=us-east -d '{"kv_prefix_cache":false}'` -> feature gate updated; rolling.

(sre-bot) feature-rollout: kv_prefix_cache=false -> 30% done.

oncall-jordan: Monitoring: error rate now 0.6% and 95p ~420ms cluster-wide. Nice. Still watching for nodes that had high OOM churn.

maria: Customer comms draft: "We observed increased latencies and errors due to an overly permissive batching config. We rolled a fix to reduce batch sizes and applied tenant-level protections. Service is stable; we'll follow up with a detailed postmortem." Want to include ETA for follow-up: 72 hours. Thoughts?

ash: good. add "no customer data was exposed" and mention compensated requests credit.

customer-alerts-bot: Sent interim notification to impacted tenant contacts (t-123, t-77, t-9).

devlin: One more change: adding a hard guard in runtime to clamp effective batch tokens per request to 8192 even if config requests higher. I'll open a PR for a hotfix that can be deployed without full rollout.

devlin: PR -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/contbatch/merge/4872 (hotfix: runtime clamp on max_batch_tokens).

maria: Thanks. Can someone summarize the immediate mitigation steps for handoff to next oncall?

oncall-jordan: Handoff summary: 
- Incident start: 1730000500 (alerts).
- Root cause: config rollout set `max_batch_tokens` and `max_num_seqs` too high, triggering kvcache growth + eviction storms.
- Mitigations applied: global policy reduced to `max_batch_tokens=4096`, `max_num_seqs=8`; per-tenant route caps for noisy tenants; temporary disable of kv_prefix_cache in us-east; fallback plan to route to distilled model if timeouts return; runtime clamp PR submitted.
- Impact: transient 5xx + elevated latency for hosted customers in us-east; peak error ~6%, now down to 0.6%.
- Customer comms: interim notice sent; PM/CS notified for credits.
- Follow-ups: postmortem, add automated canary test for large batch configs, add circuit-breaker to prevent rollout of configs with batch_token*max_num_seqs > threshold, monitor for eviction/sec > X.

ops-lead: Assigning follow-ups: 
- postmortem owner: devlin
- runtime guard & PR review: ash + devlin
- config canary & gating: samir + eng-platform
- customer reconciliation: maria + cs-team

ash: I'll review the runtime PR and try to get the hotfix build queued for a patch window (low traffic) in ~30m.

devlin: quick note: logs we saw that indicate contagion pattern: 
```
[1730000644] evict: pool=kv-us-east-1 size=1.4GB threshold=1.2GB evicting=350 entries
[1730000644] batch-retry: id=abc123 cause=kvcache-miss escalate=1
[1730000680] OOM-kill: process=cont-batcher pid=11223 mem=11.9GB
```

oncall-jordan: OK I'm handing off to ash for overnight watch. Ash, you're on pager next. Main things to watch: eviction/sec, 95p latency, host OOMs. If error rate creeps >2% for >10m, escalate to eng-runtime.

ash: Ack, taking over. I'll keep the per-tenant caps and global policy in view. Setting a watch dashboard and alert thresholds. :wave:

maria: Thanks team. Posting short incident start note to #incidents-log. Will coordinate postmortem writeup.

customer-alerts-bot: Updated status: Mitigation in place. Service stability improving. Next update in 3h or earlier if changes.

devlin: One follow-up technical note for the postmortem: we need to add a static validation on config API that rejects changes where `max_batch_tokens * max_num_seqs > 200000` (or similar) to prevent aggregate working set explosion.

ash: added to follow-ups. Also please include a regression test that simulates heavy multi-tenant clip of large prefix reuses.

ash: handing off: last check 1730001467. leaving a watch runbook pinned in the incident doc. Good job team. :thumbsup:
